svg.text: Neuroimaging studies did not get bigger — a few got enormous
1,172 OpenNeuro MRI datasets by publication year. One dot is one study. The lines are that year's 10th, 50th and 90th percentile.
anyone judging whether the field answered its own power
crisis, or sizing a study they are about to run
whether a typical neuroimaging study is any larger than it
the three percentile lines rise together, which would mean
the whole distribution shifted rather than stretched
growth over the decade, by percentile
it stretched, it did not shift
it did not reach the labs at
the line is not a pass mark
OpenNeuro GraphQL API, no key, fetched 2026-09-24; latestSnapshot.summary.subjects, restricted to datasets whose modality resolves to MRI. A year is drawn only where it holds
at least 15 datasets. Log-linear trend 1.84x per decade, t = +4.42 on 1,172 datasets. CAVEAT: a deposit archive is not a census of the field, and the 1,000-participant
benchmark applies to brain-wide association studies rather than to all imaging.
